summary:
Our tool helps a farmer compare crop rotations before committing to one. We built an open-source engine that simulates a field day by day: soil water, nitrogen, carbon, crop growth and yield. In about 4 seconds on a laptop, it evaluates all 125 three-year rotations of five crops under eight weather scenarios. For each rotation it reports yield, water use, nitrogen leaching, N2O emissions, change in soil organic carbon and stress days, and it shows the trade-offs so the farmer can weigh soil health against yield and water.

The engine is physics-based and fully differentiable, so observations can correct it. We calibrated four Iowa crops against USDA county yields and fitted a learned correction on NASA SMAP soil moisture over 40 real field parcels (2021-2024). We also selected 47 of the 148 challenge products (NLDAS-2, SMAP, HLS, ECOSTRESS, OpenET, soil surveys) and prepared them on a common 1 km grid.

As the climate shifts, past rotations become a poor guide. A fast, transparent simulator lets farmers and advisers test alternatives under different weather scenarios. It supports their judgment and does not replace it. Its skill on real fields still needs validation.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Our engine simulates a cultivated field day by day and compares crop rotations. A physics core computes the soil water balance, nitrogen and carbon cycling, crop growth and yield from daily weather and management (sowing, irrigation, fertilizer, tillage). It evaluates all 125 three-year rotations of five crops under eight weather scenarios in about 4 seconds on a laptop. For each rotation it reports yield, water use, nitrogen leaching, N2O emissions, change in soil organic carbon, stress, heat and frost days, and it exposes the trade-offs between them.

HOW IT WORKS

The whole simulation is differentiable. Crop traits are therefore calibrated with exact gradients, and a small neural correction, which starts at zero, adjusts the physics only where observations disagree with it. We calibrated four Iowa crops against USDA county yields and fitted the correction on NASA SMAP soil moisture over 40 real field parcels (2021-2023), with 2024 kept out for checking.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

Farmers and advisers can test rotation alternatives under different weather scenarios before committing land for several years. The tool supports their judgment and does not replace local agronomic expertise.

TOOLS

Python, PyTorch, uv; a laptop with an AMD Ryzen 7 CPU and an RTX 4060 GPU. Data: NASA POWER, SMAP, SoilGrids, USDA Crop Sequence Boundaries, Cropland Data Layer and county yields. We also selected 47 of the 148 challenge products and prepared them on a common 1 km grid. AI coding and writing assistants were used; the team ran all experiments.

CREATIVITY

We treat the field as a physical model that data can correct, rather than a black-box predictor. The outputs stay interpretable and every result can be replayed with one command.

FACTORS CONSIDERED

We tested the model against itself and report where it fails: fitting yield alone can hide errors in water and nitrogen, and the learned correction helps only on observed variables. Skill on real fields still needs validation.
